about: The assistant's guardrails, all in one file (Plugin build\RULEBOOK.md is their contract). The program and the hooks both read this file through rulebook.py. An owner's taught rules are layered on top from <home>\taught\rules and may only add or tighten.

rules.says: A card's state is new, yours, question, in_motion, handled or done, and a new card's kind is question, approval, task, waiting or fyi.
Only the card's own fields are written.
A card has a title; its header is its own short phrase, whole, on one line, never ending in dots, and 90 characters or less.
rules.note: A missing title is refused; dots are fixed; the length is said, not refused (today's behaviour).

rules.says: What a card needs, what it wants and why it is here are worked out by the program, never taken from Claude.
Every card cites at least one message it was given, and a closed card cites its evidence or the owner's word.
An important card says why it is important, and only what the owner's list of what matters names is important.
A new card has an area and is made only from the loose messages it was given; every card and loose message given is answered once.
A card left with the owner names exactly one thing to do or answer; otherwise it says nothing is needed.
A question already answered is never shown open again, and nothing is asked that the messages, the card or the contacts already answer.
Days are stored as dates and shown as Today, Tomorrow, Yesterday or a date.
A draft goes only to people in the card's own messages or the one person on file, with no copy and no attachment from Claude.
Only the page's own fields reach the page; message numbers and internal keys are never shown; long texts are capped.

Mail judged noise, junk, phishing or evidence never becomes a card, with one exception: a message the judge itself judged noise that neither the owner's own rules nor his Settings choices cover becomes one short "I'd hide this" card with Hide things like this and Keep showing, shown even when his setting hides cards that need nothing, one card per message, and none on a replay day; a noise verdict his own rules or Settings choices cover stays hidden with no card.
A press is a known button with valid choices; an unknown press changes nothing.

A rule card changes nothing until Approve, and a rule sentence is 8 to 300 characters, with one exception: in a kind of work the owner set to learning level 3 in Settings, the assistant promotes a rule or pick rule draft of its own with no press, only when the draft matches more of his past answers than what is in force and breaks none it matched, at most 10 rounds a time and within the RSI daily cap, and each such change is recorded in Change history and the morning summary with an Undo that puts back what was kept before it. At levels 1 and 2 the coach's change waits for Approve, and every setting or list change waits for his press.
The owner's own domains, never-junk senders and always-through people are never junked or ignored.
Plain words: no em dashes, no internal names or message numbers, every fact from the messages, and a reply recommended only when the owner is asked for something.
A card's questions are a list.

At learning level 2 or 3 the assistant does a card's pick itself only when it is Got it, Drop, Snooze to tomorrow or Keep waiting, in a kind of work the owner raised, where that pick matched what he did at least 80% of the time over 5 or more of his answers; each is recorded with Undo on its card, at level 2 with a note on the card and at level 3 in one summary card each morning; level 1 does nothing on its own.

Only four things send mail: the owner's own Send press on the page, his own words in Talk to your assistant telling it to send one email it wrote, a standing approval to send replies he accepted on an offer card, and a reply drafted for him while he has Reply drafts at learning level 2 or 3 in Settings. Claude never sends by itself.
Sending must be switched on, and mail goes only from one of the owner's connected sending accounts.
A Send press is a real press on the page, under 10 minutes old, sent once, and what goes is exactly what was shown.

At most 20 recipients counting copies and blind copies, each a plain address; subject and message not empty; attachments only files of the owner's own mail, files he added on the page or files held for that card, 20 MB together, every one fetched before anything goes.

A send under a standing approval goes only while the approval is on, only to the one person it names who also wrote the card's message, with no copy, attachment or link, 800 characters or less, from its account, within the daily limit; anything else comes to the owner.

A standing approval to send is made only from the owner's answer on an offer card, or by his raising Reply drafts to learning level 2 or 3 in Settings after the level's words say it will send; Settings can pause, change or remove it, and level 1 sends nothing.
Every send is recorded with what was sent, to whom, and what allowed it.
Phone notifications go only for important open cards under 24 hours old, once each, and wait out quiet hours.
The chat box cannot edit or run anything itself; it acts only through its listed ACTION lines, at most 8 a reply, done by the program through the same code the page's own buttons use.

An email the assistant writes goes only to the owner's known contacts or to the people on the email it answers or forwards, never to an invented address, and waits on the page until the owner presses Send or tells Talk to your assistant to send it.

A send, text or calendar change asked for in Talk to your assistant or on a card goes only when the owner's own words in that same message ask for it (never the assistant's own words), under 10 minutes old, once; an email only one already written by the assistant; and the reply says exactly what went, to whom and from which address.

A send at a learning level goes only while Reply drafts are at level 2 or 3, read fresh at the send, only a reply to the one person who wrote the card's own email, from the account it came to, with no copy, attachment or link, 800 characters or less, within the same daily limit as standing approvals, and only for a card still waiting on the owner; no other kind of work sends, and anything else comes to the owner.

The program's own files are written only by an update. The owner's own change is made as a mod or a taught add-on, only on an agreed change with the owner's clear go, its undo copy saved first, and only in the files that change names.
Into another project the assistant writes only a new file in its From the assistant folder after the owner's yes on that card, or the roadmap files the roadmap's agreement allows.
Settings change only their listed fields; sending, where the page lives, accounts, keys and roadmaps change only through a command.
Deleting is outright: a replaced or removed file is deleted, never moved to a To Delete folder; only an update keeps its own safety copies, the newest two.
No owner's name, private word, address, domain, project, calendar, area, person or account id goes into the general part.
No secret shape (a token, key, password hash, page key, session id, real page link, real address or phone number) goes into the general part.
No file of the home (keys, settings, database, logs, page state) goes into the general part.
Secrets live only in the locked key store, never in a file, page, card, log or Claude run.
The general part, the personal part, the owner's mods and taught add-ons, and the home's data stay apart, and each writer writes only where it may.
Taught connection types load after the general ones, and a general type with the same name wins.

A hidden run writes only in the home's state folder and reads only what it is given; the one exception is the run that makes a change the owner agreed and pressed go on, which writes only that change's own mod files.
Starter files are copied into the home only when missing.
